newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian conscript breaks into U.S. Moscow embassy.
newsitem.headline: Russian conscript breaks into U.S. Moscow embassy.

text.p: A young Russian who identified himself as a runaway army conscript was discovered in living quarters at the U.S. embassy compound in Moscow this month, an embassy spokesman said on Thursday.
Confirming a report in the Washington Post, the embassy said the man was unarmed and made no demands or threats before he was handed over to the Russian authorities.

The newspaper said the man, dressed in military fatigues, had broken into the home of the top-ranking American diplomat in Russia and was discovered naked in the envoy's shower after spending the night. The embassy would say only that the man was discovered in one of the compound's residential units.

The Post said that on the weekend of March 8-9 the man entered the home of the charge d'affaires, John Tefft, who is acting head of the U.S. mission. President Bill Clinton has yet to name a successor to the previous ambassador Thomas Pickering.
The spokesman declined to comment on how he breached security or what steps had been taken to prevent a recurrence. He said he could not recall a similar incident in recent years.
In 1995, mystery assailants fired a rocket-propelled grenade at the main embassy building, an imposing Stalin-era construction on central Moscow's Garden Ring boulevard. No injuries were caused.

But the embassy is less a focus of tensions than during the Cold War. In the early 1980s, the KGB infiltrated the construction of a new building, leaving it riddled with listening devices. The Americans discovered the bugs but were left with an expensive and largely useless tower block.
